primaryContext.candidateText: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.
primaryContext.fixedText: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.

context.text: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.
His return was to Ramah, for his house was there, and he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to the LORD there.

primaryContext.candidateText: “Then you will go on forward from there, and you will come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there going up to God to Bethel: one carrying three young goats, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a container of wine.
primaryContext.fixedText: “Then you will go on forward from there, and you will come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there going up to God to Bethel: one carrying three young goats, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a container of wine.

context.text: When you have departed from me today, then you will find two men by Rachel’s tomb, on the border of Benjamin at Zelzah. They will tell you, ‘The donkeys which you went to look for have been found; and behold, your father has stopped caring about the donkeys and is anxious for you, saying, “What shall I do for my son?”’

“Then you will go on forward from there, and you will come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there going up to God to Bethel: one carrying three young goats, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a container of wine.
They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall receive from their hand.

primaryContext.candidateText: Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel, of which two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the Mount of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people to their own tents.
primaryContext.fixedText: Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel, of which two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the Mount of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people to their own tents.

context.text: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years.

Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel, of which two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the Mount of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people to their own tents.
Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”

wikipediaBodyRead.supportJa: 記事はベテルを旧約聖書の地名とし、テル・ベイティンではないかと述べます。エルサレム北方・アイの西という説明はありますが、遺跡比定は断定されていません。

geography.identityCheck: 7:16・10:3は町/巡回先の直接用例。13:2は「ベテル山地」であり、都市と同じ地点の言及と断定しない。
geography.uncertainty: テル・ベイティンとの考古学的同定は記事でも推定。13:2の山地名称の範囲は不明。
